correctness.rationale: The exact 24-arc face recursion produces 1,816 nonempty simplices with f-vector (24,192,616,744,240). A 843-pair discrete-Morse matching is certified acyclic on all 6,408 Hasse covers; critical vector is (1,0,4,93,32). Exact integer gradient elimination yields a rank-one primitive d3 and zero d4, so reduced integral homology equals Z^3 in degree 2, Z^92 in degree 3 and Z^32 in degree 4, torsion-free. Original-chain mod-two ranks (23,169,444,208) corroborate. Antipodal projected ranks over F1009 split as ((11,12),(79,90),(227,217),(108,100)); they sum to the exact rational ranks, proving rational sharpness and the claimed (2,1),(49,43),(12,20) eigenspace dimensions. Both standalone verification programs were run from their delivered files.

originality.rationale: The same-object primary literature and indexed comparable octahedral and bipartite findings were compared at the statement and implication level. None gives the three-degree integral homology and central involution eigenspaces for the bidirected octahedral directed-path-forest complex. The 2022 complete-digraph result gives Euler data, not this proper subgraph homology. Direct source coverage, aliases, and broader families were screened. Unindexed overlap cannot be excluded.
residual_risks: A precise equivalent computation may be hidden in unindexed articles, theses, appendices, or unrelated terminology.

value.rationale: The octahedron is the smallest balanced complete tripartite graph and a highly symmetric canonical graph, so its bidirected path-forest complex is intrinsically motivated in emerging directed-forest topology. Its integral homology is nontrivial in three degrees with unexpectedly large free ranks, while the antipodal eigenspace signatures distinguish those classes and are not consequences of the Euler characteristic. This exact case provides a natural benchmark for cyclic complete multipartite digraphs, beyond tree and polygon families, without claiming a general theorem.
